decision: Prefer the modern ATcT energy evaluation for explicitly identified linear CCCH; retain inherited production coefficients operationally until identity and high-temperature thermal construction are reconciled.

identity.current: C3H1; label 2-Proynylidene, neutral gas, C3H stoichiometry. Neither typo nor formula uniquely proves the represented isomer.
identity.tsuji1973: Table 4 formula C3H; paper links older C/H/N/O energies to Tsuji 1964 and describes estimated structures where data were absent.
identity.modern_linear: ATcT CCCH differs from HCCCH(C3H2). CDMS identifies linear ground X2Pi_r.
identity.modern_cyclic: ATcT CH(CC) lower H0 by 7.51kJ/mol; distinct species, not an energy correction to the linear species.

source_lineage.tsuji: Numerical agreement supports FastChem annotation. It does not recover exact fitting procedure or original state sum.
source_lineage.burcat: A 7/05 G3B3 energy; Jacox 2005 plus calculated frequencies; tabulated low bent-rotor model with sigma 1 and weight 2. Historical alternative sigma 4 and 3 are explicitly noted. This is a candidate, not a validated Renner-Teller partition.
source_lineage.atct: Thermochemical network mixes experiment and theory; Costes 2006/2009 crossed beams, Garcia 2018 photoelectron spectroscopy and Aguilera-Iparraguirre 2008 theory are ancestors. Not independent confirmations of ATcT. Costes 2006 uncertainty was enlarged in the ATcT network; full original papers not read in this review.

thermal_constraints.cdms: Low vibrational Sigma component at 27.20 cm-1 above lowest Pi1/2 rotational state; v0 and one excited component catalog does not establish a complete 1500-4000 K partition. Caris 2009 Figure 4 confirms the 27.2 cm-1 lowest-level convention; its approximately 20.35 cm-1 Hamiltonian term uses the unsplit Pi zero instead.
thermal_constraints.burcat_vs_current: Compare only ideal-gas H/Cp using common NASA atomic functions. Large caloric disagreement establishes that modern molecular energy alone cannot resolve the thermal representation. No candidate abundance response or probabilistic uncertainty inferred.
thermal_constraints.isotopes: FastChem/Tsuji isotope-state convention unrecovered; Burcat mass 37.04004 is a natural-average convention; CDMS main isotopic species cannot be substituted without normalization review.

supplied_full_text.inspection: Full supplied article text read. Abstract (printed p 99, PDF p 1), Figure 4 and Table 5 (printed p 104, PDF p 6) visually checked. Figure 1 (p 100) and Section 5 Eq. (3) (p 103) identify the reference energy; the supplementary fit data are not part of this PDF and were not inspected.
supplied_full_text.redistribution: Full supplied PDF and extracted text are not vendored.

caris2009.scope: Gas-phase linear C3H X2Pi ground state and v4=1 lower 2Sigma_mu component, including their vibronic coupling; 44 pure rotational and 8 ro-vibrational transitions, 376-572 GHz.
caris2009.energy_zero: Section 5 Eq. (3) defines E relative to the 2Pi term with A_SO=0. This is not the lowest actual rotational level of 2Pi1/2.
caris2009.interpretation: The paper itself shows the 27.2 cm^-1 level separation when the lowest rotational state is zero, consistent with the rounded CDMS 27.20 entry. This resolves the apparent 20.35 versus 27.20 conflict as a reference-convention distinction, without an additional empirical energy shift.
caris2009.abstract_table_difference: The printed abstract and Table 5 report different E and beta central values. Both are retained; Table 5 explicitly defines its parentheses as one standard deviation. The cause is not established and neither set is silently substituted for the other. Supplementary fit files or a documented catalog realization are needed before numerical Hamiltonian reconstruction.
caris2009.state_model_limit: The effective Hamiltonian includes spin-orbit, rotation, spin-rotation, lambda doubling, hyperfine terms and interaction with one low Sigma component. The sign of beta is not determined from line positions; the Sigma+ assignment is assumed and linked to parity conventions. The high-J polynomial is a spectroscopic fit, not a converged high-temperature partition function.
caris2009.shared_ancestry: CDMS entry 037501 explicitly incorporates Caris et al. 2009 and earlier transition data; agreement is not independent thermodynamic validation.

follow_ups: Recover Tsuji 1964 C3H geometry, multiplicity, atomization energy and original structural inputs.

Reconstruct the low-state Hamiltonian with documented supplementary fit inputs and consistent parity/energy-zero conventions, preserving the Caris abstract/Table 5 distinction; then add and test higher vibronic/electronic coverage, nuclear-spin and isotope normalization through 4000 K. Treat cyclic thermodynamics separately.
Inspect full Costes/Garcia/Aguilera-Iparraguirre papers if adopting an energy/thermal candidate; preserve their shared ATcT ancestry.
Only then construct a named consistent candidate and rerun equilibrium with one well-defined species replacement; cyclic isomer addition requires a separate network identity.
